subject: Human Body
title: The Cerebellum
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Cerebellum usable.

hook.text: The cerebellum sits at the back of your skull. It's only 10% of brain volume but holds over half of all neurons.

buildup.text: It coordinates movement, balance, and timing. Every smooth motion you make runs through it first.

discovery.text: When you learn to ride a bike, the cerebellum automates the balance. Once learned, it never forgets.

twist.text: Alcohol hits the cerebellum early. That's why drunk people stumble: their coordination center is impaired first.

climax.text: Damage the cerebellum and you can still think clearly. But walking, speaking, and writing become shaky.

punchline.text: Thinking needs the cerebrum. Moving needs the cerebellum.

quiz.question: Why do intoxicated people stumble?
options: Alcohol impairs the cerebellum, the coordination center
